# No documented path from a clone of the engine to a running checkout

## Context

Leaf of #18985 (AC-4), authored here rather than under it because the measurement is mine and a ticket has to be one-PR-resolvable. `Refs #18985`. @neo-opus-ada keeps AC-2 (topics), AC-3 (curation) and AC-5 (review/label/spam path), and marked this one as going first: twenty curated issues behind a setup path a clean clone cannot follow is twenty curated bounces.

Hacktoberfest starts **October 1**. The contributor this door is for has a fork, Node and an evening.

## The Problem

**Every published door routes a would-be *engine* contributor into the *consumer scaffold* instead**, and the loop that actually works is written down nowhere.

| Door | What it documents | What an engine contributor gets |
|---|---|---|
| `README.md:152` → "Getting Started" | `neomjs.com/#/learn/gettingstarted/Setup` | → the row below |
| `learn/gettingstarted/Setup.md` | `npx neo-app@latest` — scaffolds a **workspace that consumes `neo.mjs` as a dependency** | the engine in `node_modules`, which is not a checkout you can change |
| `CONTRIBUTING.md` | issue etiquette and PR rules | **no build, no server, no test command** |

`CONTRIBUTING.md` contains exactly one command in the whole file — `npm ci` or `npm install` at §3.7 — and it is justified there as *"register the Husky hooks"*, not as setup. `README.md` names no install step at all.

Two further staleness defects in the same file, both verified:

- **§3.4 says *"create PRs for the dev branch and not for master"*.** `git ls-remote --heads origin` answers `dev` and `main`. `master` does not exist.
- **§3.1 leads with *"always create a new issue inside our Issues Tracker first and wait for approval"*.** That is the wrong first instruction in a month when twenty curated issues are waiting to be taken.

## The Architectural Reality

Measured on a genuinely clean clone — `git clone --depth 1 --branch dev`, then every command run through `/usr/bin/env -i` with only `HOME`, `PATH`, `USER`, `TMPDIR` and `LANG`, so no `NEO_*`, `MCP_*`, `ANTHROPIC_*` or `CLAUDE_*` variable from a maintainer shell could reach it:

| Step | Result |
|---|---|
| `git clone --depth 1 --branch dev` | 338 MB on disk |
| `npm install` | **exit 0, 3 s, 589 packages, 0 vulnerabilities** |
| ↳ `postinstall` → `neo-agent-skills-materialize` | succeeds with **no Agent OS present**: symlinks 37 skills into `.claude/skills` and prints that the directory is a projection artifact |
| ↳ `prepare` → `buildScripts/util/prepare.mjs` | runs; Husky `pre-commit` and `pre-push` are registered, so §3.7's claim is accurate |
| `npm run test-unit -- test/playwright/unit/util` | **87 passed in 671 ms** |
| ↳ with `HOME` pointed at an empty directory | **87 passed** again — and `~/.cache/ms-playwright` does not exist on the measuring host at all |
| `npm run server-start` | binds `:8082` and serves `/` and `/apps/portal/index.html` at **200**, with no build step first |
| 🔴 `npm run test-unit` (no path — the whole suite) | **exit 1, ZERO tests selected.** 41 lines of `Cannot find module '<repo>/dist/marked.mjs' imported from src/component/Markdown.mjs`, and the same for `dist/parse5.mjs` from `src/functional/util/HtmlTemplateProcessor.mjs` |
| ↳ after `npm run bundle-browser-deps` (6 s, exit 0) | **4305 tests selected, 4302 passed** |
| `npm run test-components -- test/playwright/component/button` | **exit 1** — `browserType.launch: Executable doesn't exist`, *"Please run: `npx playwright install`"* |
| ↳ after `npx playwright install` (18 s, **1.1 GB**) | **15 passed** |

**Two corrections to my own premise, both from measurement rather than reading.**

*The scary one was wrong.* I filed this expecting the Agent-OS `postinstall` to block an outside install. It does not — it symlinks and exits clean with no Agent OS present.

*The one I did not expect is real, and it is not documentation.* **`dist/` is git-ignored (`.gitignore:68`), so no clone has `dist/marked.mjs`, `dist/parse5.mjs` or `dist/mermaid.mjs`** — and `src/component/Markdown.mjs` and `src/functional/util/HtmlTemplateProcessor.mjs` import them at load. The result is not a failing test; it is **zero tests selected**, which reads like a broken checkout rather than a missing step. `npm run bundle-browser-deps` fixes it in six seconds.

**Every maintainer's working checkout already has `dist/`,** built at some point and never removed. That is exactly why this has survived: the one condition that exposes it is the one condition no maintainer is ever in.

One real wrinkle, worth a line and not a gate: `npm install` emits `npm warn EBADENGINE` on Node v25.9.0 for a dependency wanting `^22.22.3 || ^24.15.0 || >=26.0`. The repository's own `engines.node` is `>=24.0.0`, and `CONTRIBUTING.md` names no Node requirement anywhere.

The scripts a contributor needs already exist in `package.json` and none of them is mentioned in `CONTRIBUTING.md`: `server-start`, `test-unit`, `test-components`, `test-e2e`, `build-all`, `build-themes`.

## The Fix

Rewrite `CONTRIBUTING.md` so the **contributor loop comes first** and the etiquette follows it:

1. **A "Set up the engine from a clone" section at the top**, with the verified loop: Node `>=24`, `git clone`, `npm install`, **`npm run bundle-browser-deps`**, `npm run server-start`, and the test commands — each exactly as measured above, including which suites need `npx playwright install` and which do not.
2. **Separate the two audiences explicitly.** *Building an app with Neo?* → `npx neo-app@latest` and the portal Setup guide. *Changing the engine itself?* → this loop. Today the file silently assumes the second and documents neither.
3. **§3.1's approval-first sentence gains its exception**: an issue already labelled `good first issue` or `help wanted` is claimable by comment, no prior approval round.
4. **§3.4's `master` → `dev`.**
5. **A Node-version line**, since `engines.node` is `>=24.0.0` and nothing says so.

`README.md`'s "Getting Started" link keeps pointing at the app-user path — that is correct for its audience — and gains a sibling line pointing contributors at `CONTRIBUTING.md`.

## Acceptance Criteria

- [ ] **AC-1** — `CONTRIBUTING.md` opens with the engine-contributor loop, and every command in it is one this ticket measured on a clean clone.
- [ ] **AC-1b** — the loop names `bundle-browser-deps` and says **why** it exists (`dist/` is git-ignored), so a contributor who skips it can recognise the zero-tests-selected symptom rather than concluding the checkout is broken.
- [ ] **AC-1c** — the test section states the browser prerequisite **per suite**, because the three differ: `test-unit` needs none, `test-components` needs `npx playwright install` (~1 GB, bundled Chromium), and `test-e2e` is pinned to `channel: 'chrome'` (`playwright.config.e2e.mjs:69`, `:118`) so it needs **system Google Chrome**, which a default `npx playwright install` does not provide. The two live exemplars #18995 / #18996 are unit tests and must not appear to carry any of it.
- [ ] **AC-1d** — the loop builds the development theme CSS (`npm run build-themes -- -n -e dev -t all`) before the first `server-start`, and says why: `dist/` is git-ignored, so a fresh clone renders unstyled and the server only *warns*. **Added 2026-09-19 from @neo-gpt-emmy's review of PR #19000** — the original loop omitted it, and my own first clean-clone run could not catch it because the CSS in that tree had been written as a side effect of a `test-components` invocation that failed.
- [ ] **AC-1e** — the "no build needed" claim is scoped to **JavaScript**; SCSS is stated as compiling into `dist/development/css` with `build-themes` / `watch-themes` named.
- [ ] **AC-2** — the file distinguishes the app-building audience (`npx neo-app@latest`) from the engine-changing audience, and routes each.
- [ ] **AC-3** — `master` no longer appears; the named branch is `dev`.
- [ ] **AC-4** — the approval-first rule states its `good first issue` / `help wanted` exception.
- [ ] **AC-5** — the Node requirement is stated and matches `package.json`'s `engines.node`.
- [ ] **AC-6** — `README.md` carries one line routing contributors to `CONTRIBUTING.md`, leaving its app-user link intact.
- [ ] **AC-7** — the documented loop is re-verified end to end on a fresh clone with a scrubbed environment, and the run is reported in the PR body. **This is the AC that makes the others true; a prose review does not satisfy it.**
  - ⚠️ **Sharpened 2026-09-19, because the first attempt satisfied the letter and missed the defect.** Two method rules, both earned:
    1. **The clone must be uncontaminated by the verification itself.** A failed `test-components` run builds theme CSS as a side effect before it fails, so any tree that has seen one is no longer a clean rig. Re-verify on a clone that has run *only* the documented commands, in order.
    2. **Assert on the artifact the step produces, never on a status code downstream of it.** `GET /` returned 200 with every stylesheet missing. The passing form asserts the stylesheet itself (`GET /dist/development/css/src/Global.css` → 200, non-zero bytes).
  - ⚠️ **A host-provided dependency cannot be verified away by scrubbing.** `test-e2e` resolves system Google Chrome, which this host has and `env -i` does not hide — so a green e2e run here would say nothing about a contributor's machine. Where the loop depends on something installed outside the repo, the AC is satisfied by **reading the config that requires it** (`channel: 'chrome'`) and documenting it, not by a local pass.

## Out of Scope

- Curating the issues themselves (#18985 AC-3, @neo-opus-ada) and the review/label/spam path (AC-5).
- The `hacktoberfest` topic on any repository (#18985 AC-2).
- `.github/AI_QUICK_START.md` and the agent-facing §5 of `CONTRIBUTING.md`. They address a reader who *has* the Agent OS; this ticket is about the reader who does not, and the two must not be merged into one path.
- The 338 MB clone. Repository weight is #17238 / #17376 territory, not a documentation fix.
- Any change to `learn/gettingstarted/Setup.md`. It is correct for the audience it serves.

## Avoided Traps

- ⛔ **Do not document a loop you have not run.** This ticket earned that twice. The premise it was filed on (the Agent-OS `postinstall` blocks an outside install) was **wrong**, and the step that actually blocks one (`bundle-browser-deps`) was **absent from the premise entirely**. A draft of the fix that listed `test-components` alongside `test-unit` was written before either suite had been run on a cold cache; running them is what caught both.
- ⛔ **Do not delete the agent-facing section to make room.** Agent-assisted contributors are explicitly in scope for Hacktoberfest 2026 (@tobiu, 2026-09-19, #18985): `neo-agent-skills` is a published package, so an outside agent can use the skills with no Knowledge Base and no Memory Core.
- ⛔ **Do not add a per-event rule to `CONTRIBUTING.md`.** 2025 needed #7304 to take a temporary protocol back out; what lands here has to be true in November too.
